cells.location: Tirupati
cells.place: Alipiri Narasimha temple, central shrine, south, east and north wall tiers.
cells.date: Saka 1448, Vyaya, Makara śu.15, Thursday 1527 A.D., January 17
cells.remarks: Built in. Registers the gift of income from wet and dry lands to provide for the tiruppōṇakam on the day of the hunting festival and tirukkoḍit-tirunāḷ to the deity Tiruvēṅgaḍamuḍaiyār for the merit of Kṛṣṇadēvarāyar. The bhaṇḍārattar of the temple made over the gift of Chinnappa-reḍḍi, son of Sūrappa-reḍḍi belonging to Muḍiḍar-vamsa and a veḷḷāḷa of Pūttalaipaṭṭu in Muga-paṟṟu in Tuyya-nāḍu of Tiruvēṅgaḍak-kōṭṭam on the day of solar eclipse. (Published in T.T.D.I. Vol.III. No.167, pp.343 ff.).

cells.location: Tāḷḷapāka
cells.place: Slab lying in the compound of the Siddhaśvarasvāmi temple. Slab lying in the courtyard of the temple. †
cells.king: Rājēndra ‘who took the head of Vīrapāṇḍya’
cells.remarks: States that the tirukkōyil - maṇḍapa (probably maṇḍapa in front of the central shrine), nṛtta-maṇḍapa, tirunaḍil, gopura and maḍappaḷḷi were caused to be renovated and the deities viz., Ṛishabhadeva etc. were caused to be consecrated in the temple of Tenniśvaram-uḍaiyār at Periyavākkai. Also refers to the provision made for maintaining a lamp and for conducting festivals to the above diety and the other deities already consecrated. In characters of the 13-14th century A.D.

Also praises the Sarvva- siddhāchāri, the accomplished architect. Do. (Ibid.,p.164,No.C and plate).

cells.king: Śivachitta Vīra Kāvadēva- rasa ruling over Banavāsi
cells.date: Year 59, Tāraṇa, Kārttika śu. 1, Sunday, eclipse(?)
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of money accrued from tax-income by the mānisaprabhas of the village Nāghūru to gods Vināyakadēva and Viṣṇudēva and the same was entrusted to Prakāśa-tīrtha-śrīpāda of Bhōrīvaḷāparise. In characters of the 13th century A.D.

cells.remarks: This record in Sragdharā metre states that Śamva-sādhu, disciple of Pradyumna-sūri together with the guild (gōṣṭhī) caused an image of Chandraprabha to be made for (attaining) emancipation and fulfilment of his vow. cells.remarks: Bilingual. Appears to record the construction of a chhatrī on the first date by Chōdhari Lishamīdāsajī at the cost of Rs.1501. Another chhatrī also is said to have been completed on the second date by Chōdhari Gōidajī (Gōvindajī) and others at the cost of Rs.2501. cells.place: Brahmadēśam.- Chandramauliśvara temple, central shrine, south wall. North wall. †
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 90 sheep for maintaining a perpetual lamp to the deity Pōṇḍai-mahādēva of the village by Niyamankiḷān Araṅgan Pōḷandai, a veḷḷāḷa of Karaikkōṭṭu-brahmadēyam alias Parākramasōḷa-caturvēdimaṅgalam in Dāmar-kōṭṭam, a sub-division of Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḷamaṇḍalam. The shepherd who received the sheep (maṇrāḍi) Amarāyan Araṇḷi alias Tiruppōṇḍai had agreed to measure ghee for burning the perpetual lamp to the deity under the supervision of the members of kaḍaikkāṇu gaṇavāriya-perumakkaḷ. In characters of the 11th century A.D.

cells.location: CHEYYAR TALUK
cells.place: Brahmadēśam.- Chandramauliśvara temple, central shrine, south wall. North wall. †
cells.remarks: The praśasti portion beginning with Tirumaṇipivalara etc., is damaged. Records the gift of gold for food offerings during the early morning service (śirukālai-paḍi) to the deity Pōṇḍai Āḷuḍaiyār in Karaikkōṭṭu-brahmadēyam alias Parākramaśōḻa-caturvēdimangalam in Dāmar-nāḍu in Jayaṅgoṇḍaśōḻa-maṇḍalam, probably by the queen. The śrīkāryam śeyyum peru-makkal got the endowment of gold deposited in the temple treasury and undertook to carry out the endowment. Trairājya-Ghaṭikā-madhyasthan Vēṅgaḍavan Tiruvikkiraman alias Ēḷayiravan figures as a signatory. Do.

cells.date: Vikrama 1215, Pauṣa śu.10, Thursday, Rōhiṇī-nakṣatra = 1159 A.D., January 1, (f.d.n. .50)
cells.remarks: Records the making of an image of Nēmiśvara and the perpetual obeisance of the members of the Graha-pati family. Also records the perpetual obeisance of the five sons viz., Sādhu Sādhe, Sādhu Sīle, Sādhu Śānti, Sōmē and Lāle, sons of Sādhu Vāvī of the same family, to the deity Nēmiśvara. It also states that an auspicious image of Nēmiśvara was caused to be made by the illustrious and pious Jīhūla, son of Śāntinātha, who enhanced the family and who was born after the honourable Sādhu Vāvī of the Graha-pati family. (Published in Svasti Śrī, pp.138-39, 1984, New Delhi).

cells.location: ROHTAS DISTRICT
cells.place: Sasaram. Khāngāh-i-Kabiria. Slab in the western wall of the hall.
cells.remarks: Further states that Farrukh Siyar, evidently the Mughal emperor, in his fifth regnal year, made some endowment for the maintenance of the khāngāh, and Shāh ‘Ālam, obviously the Mughal emperor Shāh ‘Ālam II, in his third regnal year, conferred at-tamgha (royal grant) on account of which there was further progress (in the income of the hospice). The present building was constructed on the given date for raising the income of khāngāh and for imparting education and training to Muslim students. The work was executed by Mr.Mecanamara (McNamara) Ṣāḥib. Partly published in Tārīkh-i-Sahasarām, p.82.

cells.location: ROHTAS DISTRICT

cells.remarks: Damaged. States that Sulṭān Abū'z-Ẓafar Muḥyiu'd-Dīn Muḥammad 'Ālamgīr Bādshāh Ghāzī, after his conquest of the kingdoms of Mārwār and Rānā (of Mewār) had encamped in Deccan in pursuit of the rebellious (prince) Akbar in his 25th regnal year. He conquered the kingdoms of Bījāpūr, Ḥyderābād and Adonī and the forts of Rāherī, Satāra, Narnāla, Jinjī etc. In his 45th regnal year, when the fort of Khelna, one of the stayed in the town (qaṣba) of Bīr (and) constructed a ring of the well and water room (sabīl) at the illuminated mausoleum of His Holiness (Haḍrat Shāh Kūchak). Cf. ibid., p.26,pl.IV(c).

cells.remarks: States that this is the tomb of Maulavī Muḥammad Ghulām Qādir Khān Ṣāḥib Ṭugh Miyāna better known as Bakhshī Miyān, Advocate, son of Maulavī Muḥammad Ibrāhīm Khān Ṣāḥib, Advocate of the High court, who died of heart attack at 11 hours in the day time, on the second date at the age of forty. Further records that he came to Hingolī for change of climate from Hyderābād where plague had spread. It is also stated that the deceased was born on the first date in Maḥalla Purānā Kamela in the city of Hyderābād.
